item.text:
**Verdict:** Mostly no. The strongest 2023 evidence is that Putin preserved his regime through repression and managed a major mutiny without immediate bloodshed, but citizens were not left safer overall from political violence, displacement, or preventable insecurity. The year also saw war-related civilian harm, mass repression, and wider fear.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Russia's Putin says he let mutiny continue to avoid bloodshed | Reuters | 26 Jun 2023 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russias-putin-says-he-let-mutiny-continue-to-avoid-bloodshed-3113594 | Putin said he deliberately let the Wagner mutiny run to avoid bloodshed and said the episode reinforced national unity. This is the strongest pro-restraint item, but it is narrow crisis management rather than proof that citizens were generally safer by year-end. | 3B.10, 3B.9, 2B.5 |
| Moment: Putin says Wagner mutiny is ‘treason’ in televised address | Reuters Connect | 24 Jun 2023 | https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/moment-putin-says-wagner-mutiny-is-treason-in-televised-address/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjM6newsml_VA240124062023RP1 | Putin publicly framed the Wagner rebellion as treason and promised punishment. That shows a coercive response to a domestic crisis, not a general reduction in political violence risk. | 3B.10, 3B.9, 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Putin accuses Ukraine of destroying the Kakhovka dam at behest of West | Reuters via ThePrint | 7 Jun 2023 | https://theprint.in/world/putin-accuses-ukraine-of-destroying-the-kakhovka-dam-at-behest-of-west/1617195/ | Putin ordered rescue efforts after the Kakhovka dam breach, which is the best limited protection evidence I found. But he also blamed Ukraine and Western sponsors, and the broader event increased civilian danger and displacement rather than making citizens safer. | 3B.10, 3B.9, 3B.7, 2B.9 |
| 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia | U.S. Department of State | 22 Apr 2024 | https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia | The report says authorities jailed antiwar protesters and opposition figures, forced NGO closures, restricted media, and opened 844 criminal cases for antiwar expression. That is strong evidence that domestic safety was not improved through protection from political violence or intimidation. | 3B.10, 3B.8, 3B.6, 3B.5 |
| Russia: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023 | Freedom House says Russian authorities used excessive force against anti-war protests, criminalized dissent, and maintained a highly repressive security environment. That is direct counterevidence to any claim that 2023 left citizens safer from political violence. | 3B.10, 3B.8, 3B.6, 3B.5 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2023 | The report says antiwar rallies were brutally suppressed, police used face recognition to track activists, and protest activity shifted underground because opposition to the war was criminalized. This indicates a wider climate of insecurity and surveillance, not improved public safety. | 3B.10, 3B.8, 3B.5, 3B.6 |
| Russia crosses new lines in crackdown on Putin's enemies | Reuters via Investing.com | 21 Apr 2023 | https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/analysisrussia-crosses-new-lines-in-crackdown-on-putins-enemies-2992615 | Reuters described security services and courts as crossing new thresholds in a campaign against perceived enemies, spies, and traitors. That is evidence of repression and selective punishment, not a safer domestic environment. | 3B.10, 3B.8, 3B.5, 3B.6 |

**Search gap:** I found no credible 2023 evidence that Putin left citizens broadly safer from political violence, intergroup violence, displacement, or domestic insecurity than he inherited them. The only clear restraint evidence is the Wagner bloodshed decision, which is too narrow to offset the year’s repression and war-related harm.
